title: One move can change everything in the World Championships U7-U17
summary: With six rounds completed and five to go, every half-point counts as the race for the world titles intensifies in Roquetas de Mar, Spain. As the 2026 World U7-U17 Chess Championships reaches the halfway point, the tension is mounting across all age categories. With six rounds completed and five still to play, every half-point matters, and the pressure is becoming increasingly evident as young players face the challenge of balancing ambition with nerves. Some have established commanding leads, while others find themselves in tightly packed groups where a single mistake could dramatically change the standings. Rating favourites are fighting to stay in contention, and emerging talents are seizing their opportunities on the world stage. With Round 7 approaching after a well-deserved rest day, the players will return to the boards knowing that the final stretch is drawing closer and that the margin for error is shrinking with every move. Let’s take a closer look at each age group. Under 7 (53 players in the open section and 28 players in the girls’ section) A three-way tie at the top of the Under-7 girls’ standings sees Margad Bayasgalan of Mongolia, Leila Aldazharova of Kazakhstan, and Echo Heming Fang, representing Canada, all on 5/6, with five rounds still to play. Two of the three leaders have already suffered a defeat, while Aldazharova has drawn twice – a relatively rare occurrence in the Under-7 section, where decisive games are the norm. In the Open section, Poland’s Ignacy Mongay Miland (pictured above) is setting the pace with a perfect six out of six. He holds a full-point lead over Egypt’s Mohab Ahmed Assem, with a further seven players just behind on 4.5/6. The seventh round will see the two leaders face each other in a potentially pivotal encounter. There is still a long way to go, but a positive result for Mongay Miland would strengthen his position considerably as he looks to maintain his perfect score. Standings after Round 6 – Open U7 Standings after Round 6 – Girls U7 Under 9 (82 players in the open section and 40 players in the girls’ section) Kazakhstan’s Amaliya Yedresheva leads the Girls’ section with 5.5/6, half a point ahead of New Zealand’s Vera Jintian Xu. Top seed Stella Zhu of Finland is among three players on 4.5/6, keeping the pressure on the leaders as the tournament progresses. Mate of the day  Symbat Otargali – Varvara Volkova One of the most striking tactical moments came in the third round, when Varvara Volkova found a neat three-move forced checkmate. Her combination began with the spectacular 28…Rf1+!, followed by 29.Rxf1 Qxf1+ 30.Qxf1 Rxf1#. Black’s precise execution secured an important point. The Open section has two co-leaders on 5.5/6, with a third player just half a point behind. Latvia’s Akims Jefimovs holds a slight tiebreak advantage over Uzbekistan’s Sayfuddin Erkinboev, while Estonia’s Lev Jevglevski remains firmly in contention on 5/6. With the leaders separated by such narrow margins, the next rounds could prove decisive in shaping the race for the title. Standings after Round 6 – Open U9 Standings after Round 6 – Girls U9 Under 11 (99 players in the open section and 47 players in the girls’ section) Uzbekistan’s Akbar Mustafakulov leads the Under-11 Open section with an impressive 5.5/6, half a point ahead of a group of five players on 5/6. The 2026 Asian Champion has displayed solid fundamentals throughout the opening six rounds, dropping just half a point so far. Among his closest pursuers is top seed Amirzhan Anetov of Kazakhstan, a Candidate Master who remains firmly in the title race. In the Girls’ section, Kazakhstan’s Women Candidate Master Milana Filippova (pictured below) is setting the pace with a perfect six out of six. She holds a full-point lead over Georgia’s Sara Saltkhutsishvili, whom she has already defeated, giving her a valuable advantage in the race for the title. Filippova has already demonstrated her strength at continental level, winning the Under-10 Asian Championship in 2025. She will now look to maintain her winning streak as the tournament enters its next phase. Standings after Round 6 – Open U11 Standings after Round 6 – Girls U11 Under 13 (75 players in the open section and 43 players in the girls’ section) Women Candidate Master Lilian Schirmbeck of Germany leads the Under-13 Girls’ section with 5/6, having recorded four wins and two draws. She holds a half-point advantage over a group of six players on 4.5/6, including several of the other rating favourites. With the standings still tightly packed, the battle for the title remains wide open. In the Open section, Egypt’s International Master Abdalrahman Sameh Mohamed (pictured below) has made a perfect start, winning all six of his games. His next challenge promises to be a major test, as he faces Kazakhstan’s International Master Danis Kuandykuly, the rating favourite, who has dropped just one draw so far. Sameh arrives at this crucial encounter with an impressive recent achievement to his name: victory in the 2025 FIDE World Cup in the Under-12 category. With both players among the strongest competitors in the field, their meeting could prove a pivotal moment in the race for the title. Standings after Round 6 – Open U13 Standings after Round 6 – Girls U13 Under 15 (85 players in the open section and 43 players in the girls’ section) The Under-15 Open section is proving to be one of the most competitive categories in the championship. Kazakhstan’s FIDE Master Aldiyar Zharas currently leads with 5.5/6, but the pressure is mounting, with no fewer than five titled players just half a point behind on 5/6. Among them is Spain’s FIDE Master Martin Krauchi Romero, who remains firmly in contention as the battle for the top places intensifies. The Girls’ section is equally competitive, with three players sharing the lead on 5/6. Women FIDE Master Aiaru Altynbek of Kazakhstan, Vietnam’s Vu Nguyen Bao Linh and Mongolia’s Women Candidate Master Batkhishigt Enkhnamuun are level at the top. title: Dortmund Sparkassen Trophy 2027
summary:
By moving to the Salzlager, the tournament not only gains a new, striking venue, but also the opportunity to expand its capacity. Up to 450 active participants are expected at the Sparkassen Chess Trophy 2027. In doing so, the organiser, Initiative Pro Schach e.V., is sending a clear signal regarding the further development of Dortmund as a centre for chess.

Chess meets the Garden Show: a festival with something extra to offer

Being part of the 2027 International Garden Exhibition opens up new opportunities for the Chess Days. All active tournament participants will automatically be granted access to the IGA site for the duration of their participation. This makes the Sparkassen Chess Trophy a special experience that goes beyond the chessboard, combining sport, socialising and cultural experiences.

About the IGA 2027 in the Ruhr region

Under the theme ‘How do we want to live tomorrow?’, the 2027 International Garden Exhibition will present innovative solutions to future challenges in green infrastructure and urban development in the Ruhr region on an international stage and across three levels. The ‘GARDENS OF THE FUTURE’ section also provides the backdrop for presentations on horticulture, landscaping and plant production. The IGA Gardens of the Future are currently being created in Dortmund, Duisburg, Gelsenkirchen, Lünen and the Emscherland region.

Other local authorities in the Ruhr region are showcasing the region’s green treasures in the ‘OUR GARDENS’ section. The ‘MY GARDEN’ section gives residents the opportunity to get involved through private initiatives and collaborations. The International Garden Exhibition, featuring around 6,000 events, will take place from 23 April to 17 October 2027 – for the first time not in a single city, but across the entire metropolitan region. A total of around 3.1 million visitors are expected.

"Chess captivates people all over the world – across generations and national borders. We are therefore all the more delighted to welcome the International Dortmund Chess Days to the IGA 2027. Whether you’re sitting at the board yourself or cheering on the grandmasters as they play, this festival brings the fascination of chess to life for many people. With the salt warehouse as the venue and the blossoming ‘Garden of the Future’ right on the doorstep, chess fans can look forward to an extraordinary setting for their sport. This will be a wonderful addition to the Chess Days and to our IGA,” says Hanspeter Faas, spokesperson for the management board of IGA 2027 Ruhr."

From grandmasters to ambitious amateurs: chess for everyone

The concept of the International Dortmund Chess Days as a chess festival will remain central to the event in 2027. International grandmasters, top German players and ambitious club players will come together with chess enthusiasts from Germany and abroad. The blend of top-class competitive chess and an open, cross-generational field of participants is what gives the event its special character.

A key advantage of the new venue is that all open tournaments can be held simultaneously in the shared playing hall. This not only creates ideal organisational conditions but also emphasises the communal festival experience. Spectators can look forward to the popular live commentary on the top matches taking place on site again in 2027.

A special partnership for a special year in chess

Christian Jochmann, Managing Director of the organising body, Pro Schach e.V., is very much looking forward to the collaboration:

"Our partnership with the IGA 2027 is an exceptional opportunity for us. We are bringing the fascination of chess to a special venue, whilst at the same time opening up our festival to even more people.This is a major coup for our event and for Dortmund as a sporting hub. We look forward to working with our partners to organise a chess festival that will reach far beyond the chess community."

Further information on the 54th International Dortmund Chess Days will be published around the turn of the year. The specific tournament formats, the official announcements and the registration options are due to be announced then. Chess enthusiasts from Germany and abroad can therefore now mark the date in their diaries and look forward to further details about the chess festival as part of the IGA 2027.

Further information will be available at www.sparkassen-chess-trophy.de .
